what_happened: A retry job to define each site term once and link to it elsewhere was rejected at the final verdict. One of 7 acceptance criteria was unmet: the `cargo test -p xtask` criterion, which requires a test in xtask/src/site.rs asserting that yolo, green, red, in scope, places and home each have exactly one definition on the rendered page and that every href="#term-..." has a matching id. There were two major findings and no blockers. First, yolo, green, red, in scope and home are still defined twice on the page (in "Words used first" and in the Glossary). Red and in scope are word for word the same in studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json (start_terms and glossary; leadins.terms). Second, the test is unsound. The one-definition test counts only Glossary ids, and the 6-word test removes both copies, so neither can see the duplicate. No checks failed.
cause: The work was judged only by tests the producer wrote itself. Nothing required a test to be shown to fail on the known duplicate before it counted as proof. The one-definition test looked at only one of the two places a term is defined, and the 6-word test removed both copies before comparing. So the tests passed while the page still had duplicates. The criterion asked for a count of definitions on the rendered page, but nothing checked that the tests read the rendered page or the source data (start_terms and glossary). The gap showed up only at the final verdict, and the retry carried the same blind spot as the first attempt.
other_causes: The retry request was a one-line goal and did not say where the duplicates sit (start_terms and glossary in the intro.json files) or what the test must cover.
The data has two separate term lists, start_terms and glossary, that can both define the same word, and nothing ties them together.
open_hypotheses: The fields do not show whether the first attempt's tests had the same blind spot, or whether the producer ran the real page before finishing.
The fields do not show whether the producer tried to remove the duplicates and failed, or never edited the term data.
contradictions: The nearest class, 20261015-205707-ycg1, covers a misstated reading or mismatched provenance. Here the reading is not reported as wrong. The defect is tests that cannot see the duplicate, so the fit is partial.
No earlier case involves a site-term or duplicate-definition test, so none matches on content.
prevention: When a criterion says a test must assert a property of rendered output, the producer's brief should require two things before the job is done. The test must run against the real rendered page or the real source data. And it must be shown to fail on the known bad input, here the current duplicated terms, before the fix. A cross-check of each test against the criterion's own wording should run before the final verdict. It should confirm the test counts definitions in every place a term can be defined, not only the Glossary.
proposed_request: Define each site term once on the rendered study page and link to that definition elsewhere. The terms are yolo, green, red, in scope, places and home. Today they are defined twice: in "Words used first" (start_terms) and in the Glossary (glossary and leadins.terms). Red and in scope are word for word identical in studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json. Keep one definition per term and turn every other mention into an href="#term-..." link to it. In xtask/src/site.rs, replace the current tests with a test that renders the page and counts definitions across both "Words used first" and the Glossary. It must assert that each of the six terms has exactly one definition and that every href="#term-..." has a matching id. Show that this test fails on the current duplicated data before you fix it. Keep the 6-word repeat test, but make it compare the two copies before either is removed. Acceptance: `cargo test -p xtask`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` all pass. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
